displayedInputs.question: No common point of line \(l\) and circle \(O\) is known. To prove that \(l\) is tangent to circle \(O\), the usual approach is to

choices.A: Draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through the center \(O\), and prove that the length of the perpendicular segment equals the radius
choices.B: Join \(O\) to any point on \(l\), and prove that the resulting segment is perpendicular to \(l\)
choices.C: Prove that \(l\) passes through the center \(O\)

displayedInputs.question: \(OA\) is a radius of circle \(O\), \(OA=5\), and point \(B\) satisfies \(AB=12\) and \(OB=13\). The relative position of line \(AB\) and circle \(O\) is

\(PA\) is tangent to circle \(O\) at point \(A\), \(OA=3\), and \(PA=4\). Find the length of \(OP\).
\(PA\) is tangent to circle \(O\) at point \(A\), and \(\angle AOP=65^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle P\) (unit: degrees).
Which of the following statements about the properties of tangents to a circle is correct?

choices.A: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to any radius of the circle
choices.B: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of tangency
choices.C: Every line passing through a point on a circle is perpendicular to the radius through that point

Tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\) are drawn from a point \(P\) outside a circle. If \(PA=6\), how long is \(PB\)?
\(PA\) and \(PB\) are 2 tangents to circle \(O\), with \(A\) and \(B\) as the points of tangency. If \(\angle APB=70^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle APO\).
\(PA\) and \(PB\) are two tangents to circle \(O\), with points of tangency \(A\) and \(B\). Given \(\angle APB=60^\circ\) and \(PA=6\), find the length of \(AB\).
\(PA\) and \(PB\) are tangent to circle \(O\) at \(A\) and \(B\). If \(\angle APB=50^\circ\), then the measure of \(\angle AOB\) is
Circle \(O\) has radius 3, and \(OP=5\). \(PA\) and \(PB\) are tangents to circle \(O\), with points of tangency \(A\) and \(B\). Find the area of quadrilateral \(PAOB\).
What is the inradius of a right triangle with legs 3 and 4?
The center of a triangle's incircle (the incenter) is

choices.A: The intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the three sides
choices.B: The intersection of the three angle bisectors
choices.C: The intersection of the three altitudes

displayedInputs.question: Find the inradius of a right triangle with legs 5 and 12.
The incenter of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(I\). Given \(\angle A=50^\circ\) and \(\angle B=60^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle AIB\) (in degrees).
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=7\), \(BC=8\), and \(CA=9\). The incircle is tangent to \(BC\) at \(E\). Find the length of \(BE\).
Where is the center of the circumcircle of a right triangle?

choices.A: At the vertex of the right angle
choices.B: At the foot of the altitude to the hypotenuse
choices.C: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

displayedInputs.question: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 10. Find its circumradius.
Find the circumradius of a right triangle with legs 6 and 8.
The circumcenter of an obtuse triangle lies

choices.B: At the midpoint of the longest side

displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A=40^\circ\), and \(O\) is its circumcenter. Find the measure of \(\angle OBC\) (in degrees).
What is the circumradius of a regular hexagon with side length 2?
Which of the following statements about regular polygons is correct?

choices.A: The apothem of a regular polygon equals its circumradius.
choices.B: The circumcircle and incircle of a regular polygon are concentric.
choices.C: The central angle of a regular polygon equals its interior angle.

displayedInputs.question: An equilateral triangle has a circumradius of 6. Find its apothem.
Each interior angle of a regular \(n\)-gon is \(140^\circ\). Find the value of \(n\).
The central angle of a regular polygon is \(36^\circ\). Find the total number of diagonals of this regular polygon.
A rectangle is enclosed using \(20\ \mathrm{m}\) of fencing (with fencing on all four sides). What is its maximum area? (Unit: \(\mathrm{m}^2\))
What is the maximum value of the quadratic function \(y=-x^2+6x\)?
Use 24 m of fencing to enclose a rectangle against a sufficiently long wall (fence only three sides, with the wall forming the fourth side). What is the maximum area? (Unit: \(\mathrm{m}^2\))

An item costs 30 yuan to purchase, and 100 units are sold per day when the selling price is 40 yuan. For every 1 yuan increase in the selling price, 5 fewer units are sold per day (the price increase must be an integer number of yuan). Find the maximum daily profit. (Unit: yuan)

Use 36 m of fencing to enclose a rectangular livestock pen, with a fence through the middle parallel to the width dividing it into two smaller rectangles (the total fence length includes the partition). Find the maximum area of the pen. (Unit: \(\mathrm{m}^2\))
Given \(a/b=2/3\), find \((a+b)/b\). (Write the result as a fraction in simplest form.)
Which of the following four groups of line segments (unit: cm) can form a proportion (the order may be rearranged)?
Given \(x/y=3/4\), find the value of \((x-y)/(x+y)\). (Write the result as a fraction in simplest form.)
Given \(a/2=b/3=c/5\) and \(2a+3b-c=20\), find the value of \(a\).
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(DE\parallel BC\), \(AD=2\), \(DB=3\), and \(AE=4\). Find \(EC\). (\(D\) lies on \(AB\), and \(E\) lies on \(AC\).)
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) and \(E\) lie on \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively, and \(DE\parallel BC\). Which of the following proportions is incorrect?

The lines satisfy \(l_1\parallel l_2\parallel l_3\). Line \(a\) intersects \(l_1\), \(l_2\), and \(l_3\) at \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\), respectively. Line \(b\) intersects \(l_1\), \(l_2\), and \(l_3\) at \(D\), \(E\), and \(F\), respectively. If \(AB=3\), \(BC=6\), and \(DE=4\), find \(EF\).
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) and \(E\) lie on \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively, and \(DE\parallel BC\). Given \(AD=4\), \(DB=2\), and \(EC=3\), find the length of \(AC\).

mappings.rationale: Without a known contact point, tangency can be established by showing that the center-to-line distance equals the radius.
mappings.answerReason: If OH is perpendicular to l and OH equals the radius, then H lies on the circle and l is tangent at H. Perpendicularity alone in B does not establish that the foot lies on the circle.

mappings.rationale: The three lengths establish a right angle by the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, giving perpendicularity to a radius at its endpoint.
mappings.answerReason: 5² + 12² = 13², so OA is perpendicular to AB. Since A is on the circle, line AB is tangent at A.

mappings.rationale: The radius to the tangent line is the triangle's altitude. The isosceles altitude bisects BC, allowing a Pythagorean calculation.
mappings.answerReason: Let H be the perpendicular foot from A to BC. Then BH = 6 and AH² = 10² - 6² = 64, so the radius AH is 8.

mappings.rationale: The tangent-radius perpendicularity makes OAP a right triangle whose hypotenuse is OP.
mappings.answerReason: OA is perpendicular to PA, so OP = sqrt(3² + 4²) = 5.

mappings.rationale: Tangency gives a right angle at A, so the two remaining angles are complementary.
mappings.answerReason: OA is perpendicular to PA, hence angle P = 90° - 65° = 25°.

mappings.rationale: The task distinguishes the precise radius involved in the tangent perpendicularity theorem.
mappings.answerReason: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius ending at the point of tangency, not to every radius. A general line through a circle point need not be tangent.

mappings.rationale: The tangent creates a right triangle, and the radius is the side opposite its 30° angle.
mappings.answerReason: OA is perpendicular to PA. Since OA = 6 is opposite angle P = 30°, the hypotenuse OP equals 2 × 6 = 12.

mappings.rationale: The two tangent segments originate at the same external point, so their lengths are equal.
mappings.answerReason: By the tangent length theorem, PB = PA = 6.

mappings.rationale: The line from the external point to the center bisects the angle between the two tangents.
mappings.answerReason: PO bisects angle APB, so angle APO = 70°/2 = 35°.

mappings.rationale: Equal tangent lengths make PAB isosceles; its 60° vertex angle then makes it equilateral.
mappings.answerReason: PA = PB = 6. An isosceles triangle with vertex angle 60° is equilateral, so AB = 6.

mappings.rationale: The two tangent-radius right angles determine the remaining central angle through the quadrilateral angle sum.
mappings.answerReason: Angles PAO and PBO are both 90°. Thus angle AOB = 360° - 90° - 90° - 50° = 130°.

mappings.rationale: The quadrilateral splits along OP into two right triangles. Tangency and the Pythagorean theorem provide their perpendicular side lengths.
mappings.answerReason: PA = PB = sqrt(5² - 3²) = 4. The area is 2 × (3 × 4/2) = 12.

mappings.rationale: The target is the inradius of a right triangle. It can be obtained from area divided by semiperimeter or from equal tangent segments at the vertices.
mappings.answerReason: The hypotenuse is 5, the area is 6, and the semiperimeter is 6, so r = 6/6 = 1. Equivalently, r = (3 + 4 - 5)/2.

mappings.rationale: The task identifies the defining location of a triangle's incenter.
mappings.answerReason: The three internal angle bisectors meet at a point equidistant from all three sides, which is the center of the incircle.

mappings.rationale: The right-triangle inradius follows either from the area-semiperimeter relation or from the equal tangent lengths and the square at the right-angle vertex.
mappings.answerReason: The hypotenuse is sqrt(5² + 12²) = 13. Therefore r = (5 + 12 - 13)/2 = 2; also, area/semiperimeter = 30/15 = 2.

mappings.rationale: The incenter lies on the angle bisectors, giving the two known angles of triangle AIB.
mappings.answerReason: Angle IAB = 25° and angle IBA = 30°. Hence angle AIB = 180° - 25° - 30° = 125°.

mappings.rationale: Equal tangent segments from each vertex relate the incircle contact segments to the three side lengths.
mappings.answerReason: Let the tangent lengths from A, B, and C be x, y, and z. Then x + y = 7, y + z = 8, and z + x = 9, so 2BE = 2y = 7 + 8 - 9 = 6.

mappings.rationale: The task asks for the special location of the circumcenter in a right triangle.
mappings.answerReason: The midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices, so it is the circumcenter.

mappings.rationale: A right triangle's hypotenuse is a diameter of its circumcircle.
mappings.answerReason: The circumradius is half the hypotenuse, so R = 10/2 = 5.

mappings.rationale: The circumradius is half the hypotenuse, which must first be calculated from the two legs.
mappings.answerReason: The hypotenuse is sqrt(6² + 8²) = 10, so the circumradius is 10/2 = 5.

mappings.rationale: The task concerns the position of the circumcenter relative to an obtuse triangle.
mappings.answerReason: For an obtuse triangle, the perpendicular bisectors meet outside the triangle, on the opposite side of the longest side from the obtuse vertex.

mappings.rationale: The inscribed angle determines the central angle subtending BC, and equal radii make OBC isosceles.
mappings.answerReason: The minor central angle BOC is 2 × 40° = 80°. Since OB = OC, angle OBC = (180° - 80°)/2 = 50°.

mappings.rationale: Joining the center to adjacent vertices of a regular hexagon forms an equilateral triangle.
mappings.answerReason: Each central angle is 360°/6 = 60°. The triangle formed by two radii and one side is equilateral, so the circumradius equals the side length 2.

mappings.rationale: The choices distinguish the common center, circumradius, apothem, and central angle of a regular polygon.
mappings.answerReason: The incircle and circumcircle share the regular polygon's center. The apothem is shorter than the circumradius, and central and interior angles are not equal for regular polygons in general.

mappings.rationale: The apothem and a circumradius form a 30°-60°-90° triangle in the equilateral triangle.
mappings.answerReason: Let M be a side midpoint and O the center. In right triangle OMA, OA = 6 and angle OAM = 30°, so the apothem OM = 6/2 = 3.

mappings.rationale: Each exterior angle supplements the given interior angle, and the equal exterior angles sum to 360°.
mappings.answerReason: Each exterior angle is 180° - 140° = 40°, so n = 360°/40° = 9.

mappings.rationale: The central angle determines the number of sides, after which the polygon diagonal count applies.
mappings.answerReason: The polygon has n = 360°/36° = 10 sides. Its total number of diagonals is n(n - 3)/2 = 10 × 7/2 = 35.

mappings.rationale: The fencing fixes the sum of the two side lengths. Maximizing their product can use either a quadratic model or AM-GM.
mappings.answerReason: If the sides are x and 10 - x, then A = x(10 - x) = 25 - (x - 5)² ≤ 25. Equality occurs for a 5 m by 5 m square.

mappings.rationale: The target is the global maximum of a downward-opening quadratic. Square completion or a fixed-sum product bound gives the maximum.
mappings.answerReason: y = 9 - (x - 3)² ≤ 9, with equality at x = 3. Alternatively, AM-GM bounds x(6 - x) by 9 for 0 < x < 6; outside that interval the product is nonpositive.

mappings.rationale: Only one length and two widths require fencing, so the constraint is l + 2w = 24. The area maximum follows from a quadratic or AM-GM.
mappings.answerReason: A = w(24 - 2w) = 72 - 2(w - 6)² ≤ 72. Equality occurs at width 6 m and length 12 m.

mappings.rationale: Daily profit is unit margin times sales volume. Its quadratic maximum must occur at an allowed integer price increase.
mappings.answerReason: For an increase of t yuan, profit is (10 + t)(100 - 5t) = 1125 - 5(t - 5)². The maximum occurs at the allowed integer t = 5, giving 75 sales at a 15 yuan margin and profit 1125 yuan.

mappings.rationale: The partition contributes a third width to the fencing constraint, giving 2l + 3w = 36. The area can then be bounded by a quadratic or AM-GM.
mappings.answerReason: With l = 18 - 1.5w, A = 18w - 1.5w² = 54 - 1.5(w - 6)². The maximum is 54 m² at width 6 m and length 9 m.

mappings.answerReason: Since b is nonzero, (a + b)/b = a/b + 1 = 2/3 + 1 = 5/3.

mappings.rationale: The task tests whether four segment lengths can be paired into equal ratios, using equality of cross-products.
mappings.answerReason: For C, 2 × 6 = 3 × 4 = 12, so 2/3 = 4/6. None of the other groups permits a pairing with equal cross-products.

mappings.rationale: Dividing the numerator and denominator by the nonzero y expresses the requested fraction entirely in terms of the known ratio.
mappings.answerReason: (x - y)/(x + y) = (x/y - 1)/(x/y + 1) = (3/4 - 1)/(3/4 + 1) = (-1/4)/(7/4) = -1/7. The denominator is nonzero because x + y = 7y/4.

mappings.rationale: The equal ratios and weighted linear relation form a linear system in three unknowns. A common parameter or direct substitution reduces it to one unknown.
mappings.answerReason: Set a = 2k, b = 3k, c = 5k. Then 2a + 3b - c = (4 + 9 - 5)k = 8k = 20, so k = 5/2 and a = 5. Substituting b = 3a/2 and c = 5a/2 also gives 4a = 20.

mappings.rationale: A line parallel to the third side divides the other two sides proportionally, yielding a proportion for EC.
mappings.answerReason: AD/DB = AE/EC gives 2/3 = 4/EC, so EC = 6.

mappings.rationale: Parallel-line segment ratios validate A through C, while similarity distinguishes the whole-side ratio DE/BC from the part-to-part ratio AD/DB.
mappings.answerReason: Triangles ADE and ABC are similar, so DE/BC = AD/AB = AE/AC. Also AD/DB = AE/EC. Thus D incorrectly replaces AD/AB with AD/DB.

mappings.rationale: Three parallel lines cut proportional corresponding segments on the two transversals.
mappings.answerReason: AB/BC = DE/EF gives 3/6 = 4/EF, hence EF = 8.

mappings.rationale: The parallel cut determines AE from the part-to-part side ratio, after which segment addition gives AC.
mappings.answerReason: AE/EC = AD/DB = 4/2 = 2, so AE = 6. Therefore AC = AE + EC = 6 + 3 = 9.
